assessment.completionStatus: Successful — all six task steps completed: 255 images detected (249 , 1 CSS background, 1 meta, 2 , 2 ), 241 passing the 100×60 filter, 3/3 single flag downloads verified on disk, and a 227/227 bulk download totalling 513,626 bytes with every file decodable. Completion required two unplanned workarounds: installing the browser4-images plugin by hand and supplying HTTPS_PROXY to the backend.
assessment.successRate: 85% — every step eventually succeeded, but the first three download attempts failed 100% until the proxy was configured, and the plugin had to be discovered and installed before any image tool worked at all.
assessment.majorBlockers: 1) browser4-images was not installed in the backend (only captcha and swarm were), so every image tool was missing until I located the JAR under browser4-plugins/browser4-images/target/ and ran plugin install + stop. 2) Every download timed out with a generic 'HTTP request timed out … timeout=30s' because the machine reaches the internet through a Windows system proxy (127.0.0.1:10808) that Chrome uses and the plugin's OkHttp client does not; restarting the backend with HTTPS_PROXY fixed it instantly. 3) Rebuilding the plugin JAR from source failed in this environment (Kotlin/kapt 'Failed connecting to the daemon in 4 retries'), so I used the existing source-matched JAR.
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: A first-time user cannot tell that plugin tools exist or that a plugin is missing: plugin list shows only two unrelated plugins, tool call fails without naming the available-but-uninstalled plugin, and the discovery hint points at `plugin list` which does not list tools. Once installed, the download failures are misleading — the CLI blames its own 30s timeout while the real cause (no proxy for the backend's HTTP client) is only documented in the plugin's README. Tool names are also split between two spellings (image.detectImages in help/READMEs vs image_detect_images on the CLI), and the same download can be invoked two different ways (tool call vs an undocumented `plugin image download`) with no help text either way.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Make plugin availability self-evident: bundle browser4-images with the runtime bundle or list first-party plugin JARs in plugin list with an install hint, and make unknown tool errors name the plugin to install. 2) Fix the download-proxy trap: use the OS proxy by default in the image downloader, and align the CLI tool-call timeout with the plugin's internal timeouts so the actionable error is what the user actually sees. 3) Return structured JSON for single-object tool results instead of a toString() wrapper. 4) Report filtered-out counts (and don't silently drop dimension-less sources such as the page's 1280px og:image).

sections.body:
cd D:/workspace/Browser4/Browser4-4.14 && ./b4w.ps1 plugin list
# then try: ./b4w.ps1 -s s1 tool call image_detect_images
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.label: Expected Behavior

The only in-CLI hint is a '── Server plugins ──' note buried at the very bottom of the long `help` output.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The runtime-bundle build script (build-runtime-bundle.ps1) bundles only the browser4-swarm plugin; browser4-images is never copied into the backend's plugins/ directory, and the CLI's plugin listing has no notion of 'known first-party plugin, not installed'. The plugin's own README documents installation as a Maven <dependency> for developers, not as a CLI install step for users.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-apps/browser4-bundle/build-runtime-bundle.ps1 (plugin bundling step, ~line 985-1160); browser4-plugins/browser4-images/README.md (Installation)
sections.label: Code Pointer

- Make `plugin list` enumerate first-party plugin JARs found under browser4-plugins/*/target/ and mark them 'available — not installed' with the install command.

issues.title: All image downloads time out behind a system proxy; CLI reports a generic 30s HTTP timeout before the plugin's actionable error can surface

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s img-eval tool call image_download --json '{"url":"https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Flag_of_Nepal.svg/250px-Flag_of_Nepal.svg.png","outputPath":"…"}'
# (machine has Windows system proxy 127.0.0.1:10808 in HKCU Internet Settings; no HTTPS_PROXY env var)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The download succeeds (the browser reaches the same host fine), or the error explains that the downloader does not use the OS proxy and names the fix: image.download.proxy / HTTPS_PROXY.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Error: HTTP request timed out [tool=image_download, endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:8282/mcp/call-tool, timeout=30s, …]: error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:8282/mcp/call-tool). No cause, no hint. All three downloads failed identically; after restarting the backend with HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:10808 every download succeeded in <3s.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Two compounding causes. (1) Chrome uses the WinINET system proxy while the plugin's OkHttp client deliberately does not (java.net.useSystemProxies=false), so direct egress is blocked for the backend — documented in the plugin README but invisible from the CLI. (2) Timeout inversion: the CLI's default HTTP timeout for tool calls is 30s (cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:2149) while the plugin's per-download read timeout is 120s/60s (ImageAutoConfiguration.kt/ImageConfig), so the CLI aborts first and the plugin's own error path (which appends a proxy hint for network-style IO errors) never reaches the user.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-images/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/images/config/ImageAutoConfiguration.kt:resolveProxy(); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:2149 (30s default)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Have the plugin auto-detect the OS proxy as a fallback (or default java.net.useSystemProxies=true for its OkHttp client) so behaviour matches the browser it is bolted onto.
- When a plugin tool times out, include the target tool's own timeout and the likely cause class in the CLI error (e.g. 'backend still running image_download — downloads do not use the OS proxy; see image.download.proxy / HTTPS_PROXY').
- Default the tool-call HTTP timeout to at least the plugin's maximum internal timeout, or expose a per-tool declared timeout.
- Document the proxy requirement in the CLI help for `tool call`, not only in the plugin README.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Detection results omit the documented `type` (MIME) field on every entry

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s img-eval tool call image_detect_images > out.json ; grep -c '"type"' out.json   # → 0 over 255 entries
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Each ImageSource carries `type` (MIME), as documented in the plugin README's field list ('Each entry contains srcUrl, resolvedUrl, type (MIME), width, …').
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body: - Update the README to state that `type` is only populated for elements that declare a type attribute (/) and is otherwise omitted, or - Derive a provisional MIME type from the URL extension for entries (svg/png/jpg/webp) so the documented field is actually useful. - Consider emitting nulls explicitly (Jackson NON_NULL → ALWAYS for this DTO) so consumers see a stable schema.

issues.title: Dimension filters silently drop every source without dimensions — including the largest image on the page (1280px og:image)

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s img-eval tool call image_download_all --json '{"minWidth":200,"minHeight":120}'
# compare with the unfiltered detect list: the meta entry https://thumb.wikimedia.org/.../UN_Members_Flags2.JPG/1280px-… is absent from the downloads
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A caller asking for 'images at least 200×120' expects the page's biggest image (the 1280px og:image) to be included, or at least to be told it was skipped for having unknown dimensions.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: meta, link (favicon/apple-touch-icon) and entries carry no width/height, so the filter evaluates (null ?? null ?? 0) >= minWidth → false and drops them. The 1280px OG photo was silently excluded; only 227 entries were attempted. Exclusion is silent — totalAttempted just reads 227.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: ImageToolExecutor's filter computes `(img.naturalWidth ?: img.width ?: 0) >= minW`, treating 'unknown dimensions' as zero, which is indistinguishable from 'too small'. There is no reporting of how many entries were dropped, and no way to opt dimension-less sources in.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-images/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/images/tools/ImageToolExecutor.kt (detectImages / downloadAll filter blocks)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Treat null dimensions as 'unknown, keep' when a filter is present, or add an `includeUnknownDimensions` (default true) flag.
- Report filtered counts in the result (e.g. `totalDetected`, `filteredOut`, plus per-reason counts) so a surprising 227 is explainable.
- Alternatively fetch Content-Length/dimensions for candidate meta/link entries before filtering.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
